Thai Digital Industry Posts Quarterly Update With Few Surprises

BANGKOK — The Thai Digital Industry Association published its routine quarterly briefing this week, summarising activity across software, telecommunications, and digital services. The report tracks broad trends without highlighting any major regulatory or market shock for the period under review.

Software exports were broadly stable, growing about two percent quarter-on-quarter. The trade body said this is in line with seasonal expectations and consistent with the previous four quarters. Domestic IT services revenue ticked up modestly, while hardware imports were flat. No sub-sector recorded an unusual swing in either direction.

Membership figures changed only slightly. A handful of small new entrants joined, and one mid-sized vendor exited the local market for unrelated commercial reasons. The association noted no significant insolvencies or consolidation events during the period. Hiring across member firms remained roughly steady, with mild attrition offset by routine onboarding cycles.

On regulation, the brief mentioned that the Personal Data Protection Committee continued routine compliance check-ins and that no new enforcement actions were initiated. The Ministry of Digital Economy and Society confirmed that the existing telecom spectrum allocations remain valid through the year, with no reallocation planned. Industry representatives said no new rule changes are anticipated in the immediate term.

The report briefly referenced ongoing infrastructure projects, including ordinary-course fibre rollout and routine data-centre maintenance. Power consumption at member facilities was reported as broadly within normal operating ranges. No environmental incidents were reported. Water usage across surveyed facilities held within historical norms.

Industry observers said the briefing reflects a quiet quarter for Thai digital industry. They noted that activity is broadly consistent with the longer-term roadmap and that no immediate course corrections are required. The association reiterated that the next quarterly update will follow its usual publication schedule.
